title: Journey - Five Days of Gratitude - Day 2: Daily mercies

parts.style: warm, gentle welcome, a soft smile in the voice, unhurried
parts.text: Welcome to Five Days of Gratitude. <short pause> This is day two, Daily Mercies. <short pause> Our first sentence of thanks was, You are good. <short pause> Today we add a second... and it begins with something very ordinary, close to where you are.

Take a moment to settle. <short pause> Let whatever is holding you, hold you. <short pause> Breathe in gently... and out. <short pause> Now let your eyes or your hands find one plain thing nearby. <short pause> A cup. A sleeve. A piece of bread. A pillow. <short pause> Nothing special. <short pause> Just keep it with you for a few minutes.

Most mercies don't arrive with a label on them. <short pause> They look like groceries. <short pause> They look like water from a tap, and a bus that came. <short pause> We use them, and we wash them up, and we put them away. <short pause> And because they come so often, we can start to think that they come from nowhere... or that they come only from us.

The book of Lamentations was written by someone who had watched nearly all the ordinary things disappear. <short pause> The streets, the markets, the full tables of Jerusalem. <short pause> And it was there, with so little left to point to, that he traced what remained back to its source. <short pause> Chapter three, verses twenty-two and twenty-three.

parts.style: reverent, very slow, reading scripture aloud
parts.text: It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. <short pause> They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: It is of the Lord's mercies. <short pause> That little word, of, is doing something beautiful. <short pause> It's the word you'd use for where a thing comes from. <short pause> We are still here... and that comes from somewhere. <short pause> It comes from Someone, whose compassion has not failed once.

parts.style: gently wondering, slow, leaving room to answer
parts.text: So let's take your plain thing, and follow it home. <short pause> Who put it there? <short pause> Perhaps it was you. Perhaps someone who loves you. <short pause> And before that, who sold it, or carried it, or drove it through the night? <short pause> Who made it, with their tired and clever hands? <short pause> You will never know their names. <short pause> But see if you can picture one of them.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: Now go further back. <short pause> Before the hands, there was the stuff it's made of. <short pause> Wheat, or cotton, or clay, or a tree. <short pause> Before the wheat, there was soil. <short pause> Before the soil could give anything, there was rain, and sun, and a seed that knew what to do in the dark. <short pause> And before the seed... <short pause> there was God.

parts.style: slow, reflective, letting the words sink in
parts.text: Look at it again, your plain thing. <short pause> It has traveled such a long way to reach you. <short pause> Through fields, and weather, and strangers, and the kindness of God. <short pause> It was never nothing. <short pause> It was a mercy, all along, dressed in everyday clothes.

parts.style: warm reassurance, slow, resting between sentences
parts.text: There may be things you need that haven't reached you yet. <short pause> Following one mercy home doesn't deny that. <short pause> It only reminds you who is at the other end of the road. <short pause> The One who sent this... knows your address.

parts.style: slow, deliberate, each phrase landing softly
parts.text: So here is our second sentence, beside the first. <short pause> You are good. <short pause> This is from You. <short pause> Let's say them slowly, with your plain thing in view. <short pause> You are good... <short pause> This is from You.

Let's pray. <short pause> Father, I have received so much without turning it over to see Your name. <short pause> Thank You for this small thing, and every hand it passed through. <short pause> Bless the people who made it and carried it. <short pause> And open my eyes to the mercies I would have walked straight past. <short pause> Great is Your faithfulness. <short pause> Amen.

parts.style: soft, warm, slow sending, resting between phrases
parts.text: Before this day is over, follow one more thing home. <short pause> Your supper, perhaps, or your shoes, or the light in the room. <short pause> Go back as far as you can, until you reach Him. <short pause> And then say it softly... <short pause> this is from You.
